features.key: Looks | Sparkler A SOURCE THAT MOVES. Every generative patch before this one emits from a fixed point; here one LFO drives both the bright tip (L#, a tiny line) and the particle stream's `origin` (L#) off the same row, so they are one object rather than two things that happen to agree. The sparks are left behind because they are born where the tip WAS -- nothing draws a trail, the trail is just history. Heavy drag (#.#) and a short life mean each spark barely travels before it dies, which is what keeps the trail tight to the path instead of smearing into fog. `rate` and no `count`: this is the stream form of `particles`, not the burst form, and there is no trigger anywhere in the patch. Turn `speedVary` up and it becomes a welding torch. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Nebula Two things that did not work until recently, in one patch. FIRST, a scale-# noise field under a zoom that breathes down to #.# -- an effective scale of about #, seven times past what # LEDs can resolve. `PerlinEmitter` used to point-sample regardless of the footprint a warp handed it, so this looked like per-pixel hash the moment the zoom went low; it now fades unresolvable detail toward the mean instead, so the field goes SOFT as it magnifies rather than going to noise. SECOND, `colour.wrap` on, which is what makes the palette a ring: seven entries and NO repeat of the first at the end, because with wrap on the last entry's neighbour is the first and repeating it would give a flat spot a seventh of the wheel wide. The offset cycles endlessly on a ramp at depth #.# -- and that is exact rather than lucky, since `paletteOffset` is a Wrap parameter and a sawtooth from -#.# to +#.# wraps to the same value at both ends, so there is no jump where the ramp resets. L# is a coarse field screened over the top for depth. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Confetti Cannon Two cannons that are one cannon. The burst is fired at #.# and a MIRROR at #.# folds the far half back, so a single emitter costs one slot and reads as a pair firing at each other -- the warp is not a property of the burst and the emitter never hears about it. Coloured `random`, which is the option a spawner cannot have: each piece draws once at birth and holds it, so a burst lands as a spread of colours off an eight-hue wheel rather than a dozen of the same. A random draw does not need many stops -- the palette is reconstructed continuously, so a draw lands BETWEEN two hues as readily as on one. `colour.wrap` is on because the palette is a wheel here and a random draw lands anywhere on it, seam included. Audio drives `count` rather than brightness, so a loud hit throws MORE paper -- and because `count` is read on the trigger frame, the level at the moment of the beat is what sizes that burst. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Ember Drift Embers under a haze. Layer # is a slow noise field read through an ember palette -- the heat is entirely in the colour stage, which is the point: a fire look is a palette over a field, not an emitter of its own. Layer # is a second, finer noise field with an all-black palette blended MULTIPLY at low opacity, which mottles the embers with drifting shadow -- the premultiplied multiply is (# - alpha) at a black source, so layer opacity sets exactly how dark the darkest patch gets and nothing else. A perlin-wave LFO wanders layer #'s evolve rate so the burn is never quite steady. The two macros are the performance surface: nothing in the matrix touches what they touch, which is the rule -- a matrix row reseeds its target from the base captured at load and would overwrite a macro every frame. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Fireflies PARTICLES THAT DO NOT MOVE, and the palette doing the work `fade` cannot. `fade` only fades OUT -- a particle is born at full weight -- so a firefly built on it would pop in and then dim, which is exactly the wrong half. So `fade` is # here and the envelope lives in the COLOUR: the index is age, and the palette runs black -> dim green -> bright -> amber -> black, so a particle's whole life is one traverse of it and it glows up as well as down. That is the point of `u` being the emitter's own coordinate rather than its brightness. `wrap` stays OFF, because this palette is a gradient with two ends and both of them are black -- turning it on would join them and the fade would never complete. Everything else is a near-absence of physics: `speedVary` #.# and no gravity, so they hang where they are born. `rate` is driven by a PERLIN LFO rather than a sine, so the field clusters and thins the way a real one does instead of breathing on a metronome. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Ball Pit Objects a room can knock about. Eight balls of varying size sit at the bottom of a dim tube; a bass hit kicks the lot of them, they collide on the way up and on the way down, and they settle again on their own -- nothing has to keep telling them to. The band drives `kick` as well as firing it, so a soft hit lifts them a little and a loud one throws them at the far end. Mass is the radius, so the big ones plough through the small ones rather than trading places with them. The `L#` block underneath is not decoration: without a lit tube the balls read as sparks in the dark instead of as things in a container. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Beat Bloom The whole converter chain in one patch: continuous in, edge in the middle, continuous out. audio_band gives a level; threshold turns it into a trigger with hysteresis so it does not chatter; envelope turns that trigger back into a shaped ramp. The envelope then drives a SCALE warp, so the shape does not get longer -- the space it lives in gets bigger, and it blooms outward from the centre and settles. `expo_out` is what makes it snap rather than swell. Nothing in the flat animation set can do this, because none of them has a stage between the band and the shape. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Sine Line Port of `sine_line`: a line swung across the strip by a sine, `pos = #.# + sin * (#.# - len/#)`. THE TRAVEL TERM IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT WAS MISSING. `#.# - len/#` keeps the line's ENDS inside the strip rather than its centre, so a long line swings less far -- and it is a product of the oscillator and a parameter, which a row's fixed depth cannot express. It is two rows on one target: `M# * #.#` plus `math(mul, M#, L#.emitter.length) * -#.#`, which sums to `sin * (#.# - len/#)` exactly. A parameter is a SOURCE, so the math node reads the length the `len` knob is currently asking for; the reading is one frame stale and the length changes only when a thumb moves it. `#-sine-bass` uses the identical pair for the identical reason, and there the length is moving every frame. NOT ROOM-LOCKED, and the original is: `sine_line` is the animation `trackRoomPhase()` was written for. `LfoSignal::phase` is writable precisely so a room clock could drive it and nothing wires MeshClock to it -- LIFE-#. Two strips running this drift apart. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Prism Line (# band) Port of `prism_line`. THREE LINES ON ONE SINE PATH, which is the entire animation and which the previous port did not have at all -- it pushed three centres apart with audio and never swung them. One `lfo(sine)` is the path and every layer reads it, so the colours agree about WHEN to swing and disagree only about HOW FAR. Superimposed they sum toward white -- `add`, and not divided by the colour count, because an overlap is supposed to be bright -- and they separate into a spectrum as their amplitudes diverge. That is why the palette is primaries: red, green and blue at the same place are exactly white. EACH LAYER'S AMPLITUDE IS THREE ROWS ON ITS CENTRE, and they are three because a row has one source and an amplitude is a PRODUCT of the oscillator with a level: `M# * #.#` the swing that is there in silence -- `amp_min` `M# * #.#` `math(mul, sine, overall)`: every colour rides the overall level `M#..# * #.#` `math(mul, sine, own band)`: this colour rides its own slice Summed, that is `sin * (amp_min + overall*a + rel_i*b)` -- the animation's split blend with the loudness weighting held fixed. The animation makes the blend factor `overall * split_depth`, so how much the colours are ALLOWED to disagree itself depends on how loud it is; that is quadratic in the bands and would cost two more math nodes than the rack has room for. What survives is the part that reads: quiet is a narrow white line, loud is a wide fractured one. `split_depth` therefore lands on the three slice bands' `sensitivity` rather than on a blend factor. More gain on a colour's own band is more disagreement, which is the knob's meaning even though it is not its arithmetic. TEN BANDS BECOME THREE, the same gap `#-fft-bars` has: `SpectrumSignal` gives N outputs from one slot and is on no list in `SignalNodes`, so no document can build one (LIFE-#). The slices are the animation's own -- its ten log-spaced bands over bins #-# cut three ways, [#,#] [#,#] [#,#], which is bins #-#, #-# and #-#. Per-band auto-gain comes free: `audio_band` IS prism_line's gain staging, so each slice is normalised against its own rolling maximum and bass no longer swamps treble. `phase_spread` is #, which is the animation at rest and what makes this one path rather than three. Above # it spreads the colours evenly around the cycle -- reachable only by giving each layer its own LFO at one rate with fixed phase offsets, which is what `showcase/#-prism-fan` is. WHAT HAS NO KNOB AND WHY: `len_max`, `amp_min`, `amp_max` and `freq_max` are row DEPTHS and a depth has no address; `brightness` is the glow row's depth for the same reason, so `floor` -- its base -- is the knob that pair gets. `fall` is the animation's asymmetric peak envelope, which `audio_band` has no attack/release split for. `band_low`/`band_high` would have to re-cut three slices from one pair of numbers. `split`, the on/off, is a toggle; `split_depth` at # is the same thing. Too long for a light to keep after a restart. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Room Pulse Port of `room_pulse`: the whole strip lit, its level a raised cosine that peaks once per lap, resting at `tail` between. The previous port was a line travelling along the strip, which is what a chase looks like from OUTSIDE the room -- this animation is one light's share of that chase, and one light's share is a whole strip brightening and dimming. The pulse is `lfo(ramp_up) -> envelope`, not a sine on opacity. A sine spends the whole cycle somewhere, and `width` exists precisely so the pulse can be NARROWER than its cycle. An LFO fires on its phase wrap, so it is the lap clock, and a `smooth` envelope with equal attack and decay is a symmetric raised bump of exactly the length asked for -- smootherstep either side, which is the raised cosine to within a hair. `width` IS IN SECONDS HERE AND IN CYCLES THERE. The animation's width is a fraction of a lap, so it holds its duty ratio when `freq` changes; an envelope's attack and decay are seconds, and nothing scales one parameter by the reciprocal of another. Turning `freq` up therefore widens the duty rather than keeping it, and past about #.# Hz the default pulse no longer fits inside a lap. COLOUR ADVANCES BUT DOES NOT STEP. The animation walks one palette entry per lap, counting visits off the room clock; nothing here counts, so a slow ramp at a quarter of the lap rate glides `paletteOffset` through the four entries once every four laps, with `wrap` on so the seam blends instead of snapping. The sequence is the same; the staircase is not. AND THE POINT OF THE ANIMATION DOES NOT PORT AT ALL. `room_pulse` exists so several strips run one animation in step off `MeshClock`, a chase set up by a single broadcast with nothing to drop. There is no room-clock source (LIFE-#), so two devices running this drift apart and it is simply a pulsing light -- which is, to be fair, exactly what the animation degrades to on a device that has never heard a Master. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Mirror Brush Port of `mirror_brush`: a brush that paints while the room is loud, and whatever it painted scrolls outward from the centre, mirrored. features.key: Looks | Audio Fireworks Port of `fireworks_audio`, which is `fireworks` with the launch clock replaced by a beat. The previous port was one particle layer with no rocket at all. THE WHOLE CHAIN IS ONE BEAT FANNED OUT. `audio_band` -> `threshold` is the beat; that edge then does three separate jobs: - it triggers the rocket spawner directly; - it RESTARTS a `sample_hold` LFO at rate # (LIFE-#), which is sample-and-hold proper -- a new height drawn on the hit and only on the hit, so the rocket's launch speed is set the moment it leaves; - it enters a `delay` whose Time is the flight time, carrying that same height on its second wire. The delay's edge is the burst, and its value is where the burst goes. EVERY BEAT GETS ITS OWN BURST, and that is what the delay is for (LIFE-#). The first cut timed the flight with `envelope -> threshold`, and an envelope has one voice: a beat arriving mid-flight restarted it, and the rocket already in the air ran out its life with nothing left to explode it. At # BPM that was thirteen beats and zero bursts. A delay queues each edge on its own, so a new beat starts another flight instead of cancelling the one in the air. The carried height matters just as much: by the time beat #'s burst is due, beat # has already redrawn the `sample_hold`, so a burst reading it directly would land on the wrong rocket. What the delay publishes is the value it read when THAT beat arrived. THE BURST LANDS WHERE THE ROCKET IS, by construction rather than by authoring, and the arithmetic is `#-fireworks`'s. A spawner with `acceleration` # and drag `d` asymptotes at `velocity / d`, so bursting at a fixed fraction `f` of that asymptote takes `-ln(# - f) / d` seconds whatever the launch speed -- which is why ONE delay time is right for a low shot and a high one alike. Bursting at #% keeps the shell moving at #% of launch speed right up to the frame it goes, instead of creeping toward an apex it never reaches. So the burst zone [#.#, #.#] -- this animation's `burst_min`/`burst_max`, higher than the unreactive one's -- means an asymptote of `(#.# + #.#h)/#.#`, hence velocity base #.# and depth #.# against drag #.#, and a flight of `-ln(#.#)/#.#` = #.# s. THE ROCKET IS STILL LIT WHEN IT BURSTS. `lifetime` #.# with `fadeOut` #.# starts the fade at #.# s, the burst frame, so the shell is at full weight up to the flash and dies into it over the next # ms. An earlier cut had the fade ENDING near the burst, which left a #%-bright ember to explode and read as a rocket vanishing before its own sparks. `colouring: speed` against a `speedRef` that tracks the launch speed is exactly the animation's `brightness = speedFrac`. `maxAlive` is # because flights now overlap: at a fast tempo two or three rockets are in the air at once, and a cap of # would retire one that still had a burst on its way. WHERE IT DIVERGES, and it is the trigger rather than the look: the animation bursts every rocket in flight on the NEXT beat, or at the apex if that comes first, and this bursts each one a fixed flight-time after its own beat. Nothing in the engine turns "this shape died" into an edge -- the same gap `#-fireworks` records. The animation's flight is `sqrt(#*target/decel)`, #.#-#.# s; this one's #.# s is the nearest the velocity/drag geometry reaches with one fixed time. Where the animation cuts a rocket short on a fast beat, this lets it finish, so at a quick tempo there are more shells in the air at once than the animation would show. `beat_thresh` and `avg_decay` change UNITS here. With the delay it is no longer needed to keep bursts alive, which was the only thing going wrong without it. The spark knobs are `#-fireworks`'s rows and rest on its tuned values for its reasons; `num_sparks` also stops at # rather than the animation's #, because that is where `particles.count` stops. features.key: Looks | Fireworks Port of `fireworks`. THE BURST LANDS WHERE THE ROCKET STOPPED, and that is not authored: a spawner with `acceleration` # and drag d covers `velocity / d`, so ONE sample_hold LFO drives the rocket's `velocity` AND the burst's `origin` and the two agree by construction. Each shot picks its own height in [#.#, #.#], which is `burst_min`/`burst_max`. What makes a fixed clock offset legal: the time to reach a given FRACTION of that distance depends on d alone and not on the launch speed, so the burst fires #.# s after the launch whether the shot went low or high. IT BURSTS AT #% AND NOT AT THE TOP, which is the correction that matters most: the original decelerates LINEARLY and stops dead, while drag is exponential and only ever asymptotes, so a rocket allowed to run to its apex creeps for half a second at nearly nothing and reads as a smear drifting up the strip. Bursting early keeps it moving at #% of launch speed right up to the frame it dies, and `lifetime` #.# cuts it on that frame rather than fading it into the burst. THE SECOND THING THAT HAD TO BE TUNED BY EYE IS THE FLIGHT TIME. Drag is what sets it, and at #.# the rocket crossed half the strip in a third of a second and read as a flick rather than a launch; #.# puts it at #.# s, inside the #.#-#.# s the original's `decel` #.# gives. `speedRef` rides the same held number as `velocity`, which is the original's `speedFrac = |vel| / launchSpeed` exactly -- normalised against ITS OWN launch speed, so a low shot is dim from slowing rather than from never having been fast. `flicker` is M#/M# on the rocket layers' opacity, #.# +/- #.#, which is the original's `# - flicker + flicker * (#.# + #.# sin)` at its default #.# -- and it is honest here only because `maxAlive` is #, so a LAYER-wide flicker is a per-rocket flicker. Two rates rather than one so the pair does not pulse together. TWO LAUNCHERS, opposite ends, #.# and #.# Hz -- the original picks an end at random and one clock cannot, and the incommensurate rates stop the pair beating into a rhythm. SPARKS ARE THIN AND WIDE, and that pairing is the whole of it. `PointSet::sample` CLAMPS summed density at # and blends the `u` of everything overlapping, where the original sums colours -- so two overlapping sparks here become one saturated blob of averaged colour rather than a brighter pair. The original's own numbers (bloom #.#, # sparks) therefore do not port: at # LEDs that is a #.#-LED spark and a burst arrives as a solid bar. features.key: Looks | Picket One `line` that never moves, drawn as a moving fence. `tile` turns a single shape into N copies, `translate` slides the tiled coordinate so the whole set travels, and `mirror` folds it so the fence approaching from one side meets itself coming back. Three warps, all modulated, on an emitter whose `centre` is #.# for the entire patch -- every bit of motion you see is the space moving under a stationary object, which is the cheapest complex animation the engine can produce: one trapezoid integration per pixel however many pickets the tile makes. The count is on a triangle from three to eleven and it is a float, so between integers the last cell is cut short and a discontinuity travels through the fence once per integer crossed. That is the same artefact `#-phaser` uses deliberately; here it reads as a post being added or removed while you watch. The chain is `M# -> M#.rate`, so the scroll surges and stalls rather than running at a constant speed, and the fence occasionally hangs almost still while the count is still changing under it. `index: "position"` means the palette is fixed to the STRIP rather than to the pickets, so a post changes colour as it travels rather than carrying one -- the fence is a moving window onto a stationary gradient. Ember run with a single cobalt accent that only the far end of the strip holds. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | VU Peak Hold The bar and the marker that hangs above it. There is no peak-hold node and there does not need to be: two `audio_band` sources on the SAME bins with wildly different `smoothing` are a fast reading and a slow one, and a slow follower above a fast bar is what a peak hold looks like. #.# s against #.# s -- the top of the declared range -- plus `slew` #.# on the slow one, so it falls at a fixed speed rather than decaying exponentially. features.key: Looks | Room Pulse Port of `room_pulse`: the whole strip lit, its level a raised cosine that peaks once per lap, resting at `tail` between. The previous port was a line travelling along the strip, which is what a chase looks like from OUTSIDE the room -- this animation is one light's share of that chase, and one light's share is a whole strip brightening and dimming. The pulse is `lfo(ramp_up) -> envelope`, not a sine on opacity. A sine spends the whole cycle somewhere, and `width` exists precisely so the pulse can be NARROWER than its cycle. An LFO fires on its phase wrap, so it is the lap clock, and a `smooth` envelope with equal attack and decay is a symmetric raised bump of exactly the length asked for -- smootherstep either side, which is the raised cosine to within a hair. `width` IS IN SECONDS HERE AND IN CYCLES THERE. The animation's width is a fraction of a lap, so it holds its duty ratio when `freq` changes; an envelope's attack and decay are seconds, and nothing scales one parameter by the reciprocal of another. Turning `freq` up therefore widens the duty rather than keeping it, and past about #.# Hz the default pulse no longer fits inside a lap. COLOUR ADVANCES BUT DOES NOT STEP. The animation walks one palette entry per lap, counting visits off the room clock; nothing here counts, so a slow ramp at a quarter of the lap rate glides `paletteOffset` through the four entries once every four laps, with `wrap` on so the seam blends instead of snapping. The sequence is the same; the staircase is not. AND THE POINT OF THE ANIMATION DOES NOT PORT AT ALL. `room_pulse` exists so several strips run one animation in step off `MeshClock`, a chase set up by a single broadcast with nothing to drop. There is no room-clock source (LIFE-#), so two devices running this drift apart and it is simply a pulsing light -- which is, to be fair, exactly what the animation degrades to on a device that has never heard a Master.

features.key: Looks | Prism Line (# band) Port of `prism_line`. THREE LINES ON ONE SINE PATH, which is the entire animation and which the previous port did not have at all -- it pushed three centres apart with audio and never swung them. One `lfo(sine)` is the path and every layer reads it, so the colours agree about WHEN to swing and disagree only about HOW FAR. Superimposed they sum toward white -- `add`, and not divided by the colour count, because an overlap is supposed to be bright -- and they separate into a spectrum as their amplitudes diverge. That is why the palette is primaries: red, green and blue at the same place are exactly white. EACH LAYER'S AMPLITUDE IS THREE ROWS ON ITS CENTRE, and they are three because a row has one source and an amplitude is a PRODUCT of the oscillator with a level: `M# * #.#` the swing that is there in silence -- `amp_min` `M# * #.#` `math(mul, sine, overall)`: every colour rides the overall level `M#..# * #.#` `math(mul, sine, own band)`: this colour rides its own slice Summed, that is `sin * (amp_min + overall*a + rel_i*b)` -- the animation's split blend with the loudness weighting held fixed. The animation makes the blend factor `overall * split_depth`, so how much the colours are ALLOWED to disagree itself depends on how loud it is; that is quadratic in the bands and would cost two more math nodes than the rack has room for. What survives is the part that reads: quiet is a narrow white line, loud is a wide fractured one. `split_depth` therefore lands on the three slice bands' `sensitivity` rather than on a blend factor. More gain on a colour's own band is more disagreement, which is the knob's meaning even though it is not its arithmetic. TEN BANDS BECOME THREE, the same gap `#-fft-bars` has: `SpectrumSignal` gives N outputs from one slot and is on no list in `SignalNodes`, so no document can build one (LIFE-#). The slices are the animation's own -- its ten log-spaced bands over bins #-# cut three ways, [#,#] [#,#] [#,#], which is bins #-#, #-# and #-#. Per-band auto-gain comes free: `audio_band` IS prism_line's gain staging, so each slice is normalised against its own rolling maximum and bass no longer swamps treble. `phase_spread` is #, which is the animation at rest and what makes this one path rather than three. Above # it spreads the colours evenly around the cycle -- reachable only by giving each layer its own LFO at one rate with fixed phase offsets, which is what `showcase/#-prism-fan` is. WHAT HAS NO KNOB AND WHY: `len_max`, `amp_min`, `amp_max` and `freq_max` are row DEPTHS and a depth has no address; `brightness` is the glow row's depth for the same reason, so `floor` -- its base -- is the knob that pair gets. `fall` is the animation's asymmetric peak envelope, which `audio_band` has no attack/release split for. `band_low`/`band_high` would have to re-cut three slices from one pair of numbers. `split`, the on/off, is a toggle; `split_depth` at # is the same thing. Too long for a light to keep after a restart.

THE BURST LANDS WHERE THE ROCKET STOPPED, and that is not authored: a spawner with `acceleration` # and drag d covers `velocity / d`, so ONE sample_hold LFO drives the rocket's `velocity` AND the burst's `origin` and the two agree by construction. IT BURSTS AT #% AND NOT AT THE TOP, which is the correction that matters most: the original decelerates LINEARLY and stops dead, while drag is exponential and only ever asymptotes, so a rocket allowed to run to its apex creeps for half a second at nearly nothing and reads as a smear drifting up the strip. Bursting early keeps it moving at #% of launch speed right up to the frame it dies, and `lifetime` #.# cuts it on that frame rather than fading it into the burst. THE SECOND THING THAT HAD TO BE TUNED BY EYE IS THE FLIGHT TIME. Drag is what sets it, and at #.# the rocket crossed half the strip in a third of a second and read as a flick rather than a launch; #.# puts it at #.# s, inside the #.#-#.# s the original's `decel` #.# gives. `speedRef` rides the same held number as `velocity`, which is the original's `speedFrac = |vel| / launchSpeed` exactly -- normalised against ITS OWN launch speed, so a low shot is dim from slowing rather than from never having been fast. `flicker` is M#/M# on the rocket layers' opacity, #.# +/- #.#, which is the original's `# - flicker + flicker * (#.# + #.# sin)` at its default #.# -- and it is honest here only because `maxAlive` is #, so a LAYER-wide flicker is a per-rocket flicker. The animation's level is `floor + (#-floor) * #.# * (# - cos(#*pi*phase))`; a sine row folded unipolar gives `#.# + #.#*sin`, so base opacity #.# with depth #.# and `bipolar: false` is the same curve, and the LFO's `phase` chooses where in it the strip starts. `effect` IS A SELECT AND A MACRO IS A SCALAR, so it becomes the breathe RATE: # is `solid` and anything above it is `breathe` at that speed. features.key: Looks | Mirror Brush Port of `mirror_brush`: a brush that paints while the room is loud, and whatever it painted scrolls outward from the centre, mirrored. The previous port was one line under a mirror on a triangle LFO, which is a shape bouncing rather than a trail being laid down. A STROKE IS ONE SUSTAINED SPAWN. The animation keeps a segment per stroke: its outer edge is where the scroll stood when the brush went down, and its inner edge is re-pinned to the centre every frame the brush stays down, then released when it lifts. That is `spawner.sustain` exactly -- the leading end launches on the threshold's rising edge, the trailing end holds at the origin while the threshold is `held()`, and the dip lets it go. So a loud bar paints one unbroken band rather than a row of dots, and a gap in the music is a gap in the trail. An earlier revision of this port streamed `particles` at a rate the band drove, which painted density rather than strokes. `threshold` is the trip level of a `threshold` node on the band, with hysteresis # because the animation compares `smoothed > threshold` with none. The band's own squelch stays at # so the two are not stacked. `mirror` maps a screen position to `|pos - centre| * #`, so the emitter works in a half-strip where source # is the middle and source # is both ends. Every distance doubles with it: the animation's `min_speed` of #.# strip/s is a Launch Speed of #.# in this space, and the knob's ends are its declared #.#-# doubled. Acceleration and drag are # because the animation scrolls at a constant speed, so a released stroke keeps its length. Lifetime # retires a stroke once it has left the end, which is the animation's `scroll - endScroll > #.# + bloom`. The animation's own comment says it folds with `abs(pos - #.#)`; this is that fold as a warp. `colors` cycling one entry per stroke becomes `colouring: index`, which also advances once per stroke and in a fixed rotation. features.key: Looks | Arpeggio A note jumps between positions and its COLOUR comes from where it landed, not from anything about the note. That is `index: "position"` used as a keyboard -- the palette is laid once along the strip and a line stepping through it plays it like a scale. The line carries no colour of its own; it reveals one already there, which is the distinction `showcase/#-ladder` draws between Position and U, put to work. The steps are a `sample_hold` at a small non-zero `slew`: #.# s is about six frames at # FPS, fast enough to still read as a step and slow enough that the eye follows it. Two chains stack. The draw drives `M#.rate` -- a second, slower sequencer whose tempo is set by the last note. Note what LIFE-# means here: `LfoSignal::seed` is not in the document, so both `sample_hold` sources draw the IDENTICAL sequence. They are not two independent players. features.key: Looks | Sunset The strip is a sky. A `block` coloured by POSITION lays a gradient along it -- orange at the horizon end through red and rose to violet and indigo -- with `paletteSpan` #.#, so the strip only ever shows sixty percent of that sky. A sine at #.# Hz slides `paletteOffset` through the other forty: the window starts on the warm end and walks to the cold one, which is the sun going down, then walks back. At Speed # % one full dusk-and-return takes about # minutes; the knob runs it from about # minutes to over an hour. Nothing in a patch can read the wall clock, so it begins wherever the sine is when the patch starts -- the phase is set so that is sunset, not midnight. The same slow clock sinks the sun: a soft glint near the horizon end that slides further down and fades as the sky cools. Clouds are a noise layer with a black palette blended `multiply`, which dims by its own alpha and so darkens the sky in drifting bands -- the trick `downpour` uses for its gusts. Plays on Left, Right only

Nothing pulses on a beat. Silence reads #, eased, so a room that goes quiet slows back to its own pace rather than stopping. The one thing the rhythm does touch is the colour, once a bar: a `beat` on every bar widens the hue `spread` of a recolour row on the aurora and lets it settle, so on each downbeat the greens fan out towards blue and violet along the strip and gather again. features.key: Looks | Ricochet Shapes launched from one end that bounce off the middle of the strip. There is no collision here and nothing in `SpawnerEmitter` knows what a wall is -- `mirror` folds the coordinate about its centre, so a shape crossing that point re-emerges travelling the other way. `MirrorWarp::toSource` is `|pos - centre| * #`, which means the reflection is EXACT and free, and it costs one warp. The mirror's `centre` is on a slow triangle, so the wall moves. A shape launched while the wall is far travels most of the strip before turning; one launched while it is near turns almost immediately. Same emitter, same velocity, completely different flight -- and because the wall keeps moving while a shape is in the air, the turn happens somewhere neither the launch nor the wall alone determines. The chain is `M# -> M#.rate`, the launch clock on a noise source, so shots arrive in bursts and gaps rather than on a beat. `colouring: "speed"` with `drag` #.# means each shape is born hot and cools as it slows, so you can read how long ago a thing was fired from its colour alone. Split complement: cerise and violet for the shapes with acid lime # degrees away on the wall glow, which is the only thing marking where the fold currently is. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Starfield A night sky: stars that fade in, hold and fade out where they are, over a faint deep-blue sky, with a shooting star every so often. The stars are `particles` with no speed, no gravity and `fade` #, because fade only fades OUT and a star has to come up as well. The twinkle lives in the colour instead, as in `#-foxfire`: coloured by AGE through a palette that starts and ends black, so each star's whole life is one rise and fall. The palette is left unboosted on purpose -- saturation # would turn the near-white entries into pure hues, and stars are white. A perlin LFO on the birth rate clusters them; a slower perlin varies that one's rate. The shooting star is `downpour`'s lightning chain with a shape where the flash was: a `sample_hold` draw has to clear #.# to trip the threshold, about one draw in thirteen at a quarter-hertz, so a streak arrives every minute or so and never on a schedule. The same draw sets where it starts. Its tail is a `fade` warp listed ABOVE the colour row, so the palette colours the tail as it decays -- white at the head, blue behind. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Coals The fire after it has burned down. A dim crimson bed that barely moves, and over it a second, finer noise whose palette is BLACK for most of its range -- black here means off -- so only its crests light, glowing orange-to-gold where the coals are hottest. Heat is that layer's `indexBias`: turn it up and more of each coal catches. The crests breathe on a slow sine into the same `indexBias`, and a perlin LFO drives that sine's rate, so the glow swells and settles irregularly instead of on a count. A fast, shallow perlin shimmers the crest layer's opacity -- heat haze, not flicker. The bed and the crests drift in opposite directions at very different speeds, so the hot spots slide over the embers rather than sitting on them.

features.key: Looks | Prism Fan `#-prism` with five clocks instead of one. Each line gets its own sine LFO at the same rate and a phase a fifth of a turn ahead of the one before it -- M#..M# at #.#, #.#, #.#, #.#, #.# driving L#..L# in order -- so the five sweeps run as one travelling wave rather than in unison. Identical rates are what keeps the stagger: the offsets are set once and never drift, because nothing pulls the rates apart. The sweep is a `translate` warp, not the emitter's `centre`, and that is the load-bearing choice. `offset` has a base of ZERO, and a `multiply` row does `*= (# + v * depth)` -- so a row multiplying an offset scales the swing and leaves the line's home alone. Multiplying `centre` would have dragged all five toward p=# instead. The emitter centre is now only where a line lives; the warp is how far it travels. **A matrix row's `depth` has no address**, so no rack knob can reach the five of them, and `Macro::MAX_TARGETS` is # in any case -- the same wall that left `#-prism` with one knob. `M#` is the way round it: a `macro` signal is a plain #..# matrix SOURCE, so one rack control fans out to five multiply rows through a single target. The LFO rows carry #.# and the multiply rows #.#, which puts the swing at #.# with the knob down and #.# -- `#-prism`'s figure -- with it up. Unity at zero is inherent to `# + v*depth`, so a knob like this scales an amplitude the document chose; it cannot start one from nothing. And because the knob is a modulator parameter rather than a rack entry, the audio band can drive it: `M#` adds bass onto `M#.knob` and the whole fan opens on the beat, one knob upstream of five rows. A row reads its source before a later row writes it, so the bass lands a frame late -- # ms at # FPS. `screen` rather than `add`: five saturated lines at value #.# crossing under `add` spend their time clipped white, and the crossings are the point. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Ricochet Shapes launched from one end that bounce off the middle of the strip. There is no collision here and nothing in `SpawnerEmitter` knows what a wall is -- `mirror` folds the coordinate about its centre, so a shape crossing that point re-emerges travelling the other way. `MirrorWarp::toSource` is `|pos - centre| * #`, which means the reflection is EXACT and free, and it costs one warp. The mirror's `centre` is on a slow triangle, so the wall moves. A shape launched while the wall is far travels most of the strip before turning; one launched while it is near turns almost immediately. Same emitter, same velocity, completely different flight -- and because the wall keeps moving while a shape is in the air, the turn happens somewhere neither the launch nor the wall alone determines. The chain is `M# -> M#.rate`, the launch clock on a noise source, so shots arrive in bursts and gaps rather than on a beat. `colouring: "speed"` with `drag` #.# means each shape is born hot and cools as it slows, so you can read how long ago a thing was fired from its colour alone. Split complement: cerise and violet for the shapes with acid lime # degrees away on the wall glow, which is the only thing marking where the fold currently is.

features.key: Looks | Starfield A night sky: stars that fade in, hold and fade out where they are, over a faint deep-blue sky, with a shooting star every so often. The stars are `particles` with no speed, no gravity and `fade` #, because fade only fades OUT and a star has to come up as well. The twinkle lives in the colour instead, as in `#-foxfire`: coloured by AGE through a palette that starts and ends black, so each star's whole life is one rise and fall. The palette is left unboosted on purpose -- saturation # would turn the near-white entries into pure hues, and stars are white. A perlin LFO on the birth rate clusters them; a slower perlin varies that one's rate. The shooting star is `downpour`'s lightning chain with a shape where the flash was: a `sample_hold` draw has to clear #.# to trip the threshold, about one draw in thirteen at a quarter-hertz, so a streak arrives every minute or so and never on a schedule. The same draw sets where it starts. Its tail is a `fade` warp listed ABOVE the colour row, so the palette colours the tail as it decays -- white at the head, blue behind.

features.key: Looks | Sunset The strip is a sky. A `block` coloured by POSITION lays a gradient along it -- orange at the horizon end through red and rose to violet and indigo -- with `paletteSpan` #.#, so the strip only ever shows sixty percent of that sky. A sine at #.# Hz slides `paletteOffset` through the other forty: the window starts on the warm end and walks to the cold one, which is the sun going down, then walks back. At Speed # % one full dusk-and-return takes about # minutes; the knob runs it from about # minutes to over an hour. Nothing in a patch can read the wall clock, so it begins wherever the sine is when the patch starts -- the phase is set so that is sunset, not midnight. The same slow clock sinks the sun: a soft glint near the horizon end that slides further down and fades as the sky cools. Clouds are a noise layer with a black palette blended `multiply`, which dims by its own alpha and so darkens the sky in drifting bands -- the trick `downpour` uses for its gusts.

features.key: Looks | Mirror Brush Port of `mirror_brush`: a brush that paints while the room is loud, and whatever it painted scrolls outward from the centre, mirrored. The previous port was one line under a mirror on a triangle LFO, which is a shape bouncing rather than a trail being laid down. A TRAIL IS PARTICLES WITH A RATE, not a spawner with a trigger. `particles.rate` is a continuous stream in shapes per second, carried across frames so it means the same at # FPS as at #, and the audio band drives it -- so loud paints densely, quiet paints nothing, and the brush going down and up is the band crossing its squelch. That is what makes `threshold` a real knob here: it IS the squelch. `mirror` maps a screen position to `|pos - centre| * #`, so the emitter works in a half-strip where source # is the middle and source # is both ends. Every distance doubles with it: the animation's `min_speed` of #.# strip/s is #.# in this space, and the knob's ends are its declared #.#-# doubled. The animation's own comment says it folds with `abs(pos - #.#)`; this is that fold as a warp. `colors` cycling one entry per stroke becomes `colouring: random`, a draw held for the life of each particle. Consecutive strokes therefore differ, but not in the animation's fixed rotation. `react_speed` and `react_brightness` are toggles and do not port, for the reason `#-perlin-audio` gives -- both default false, so this takes the constant each selects and the reaction lands on density instead. `max_speed` is then the depth of a row that is not there. `bloom` is the animation's falloff either side of a painted SEGMENT and here it is a particle's whole half-extent, which is a different measurement of the same softness. Plays on Left, Right only

Each line gets its own sine LFO at the same rate and a phase a fifth of a turn ahead of the one before it -- M#..M# at #.#, #.#, #.#, #.#, #.# driving L#..L# in order -- so the five sweeps run as one travelling wave rather than in unison. Identical rates are what keeps the stagger: the offsets are set once and never drift, because nothing pulls the rates apart. The sweep is a `translate` warp, not the emitter's `centre`, and that is the load-bearing choice. `offset` has a base of ZERO, and a `multiply` row does `*= (# + v * depth)` -- so a row multiplying an offset scales the swing and leaves the line's home alone. Multiplying `centre` would have dragged all five toward p=# instead. The emitter centre is now only where a line lives; the warp is how far it travels. **A matrix row's `depth` has no address**, so no rack knob can reach the five of them, and `Macro::MAX_TARGETS` is # in any case -- the same wall that left `#-prism` with one knob. `M#` is the way round it: a `macro` signal is a plain #..# matrix SOURCE, so one rack control fans out to five multiply rows through a single target. The LFO rows carry #.# and the multiply rows #.#, which puts the swing at #.# with the knob down and #.# -- `#-prism`'s figure -- with it up. Unity at zero is inherent to `# + v*depth`, so a knob like this scales an amplitude the document chose; it cannot start one from nothing. features.key: Looks | Kick Comet Every kick launches one shape from the near end and the strip is whatever is still in flight. The trigger is a `threshold` on the bass band, and `hysteresis` at #.# is what makes it a beat detector rather than a buzzer -- without it a sustained note re-crosses its own ripple dozens of times a second and the comets never separate. The envelope beside it drives nothing visual. It sets the comet's `velocity`, so a hard kick throws a fast one and a soft kick a slow one. Nothing in `SpawnerEmitter` reads velocity after birth, so the value at the instant of the trigger is the one the shape keeps for life -- the envelope is being SAMPLED rather than followed, which is what `ports/#-fireworks` does with a `sample_hold` for the same reason. `drag` #.# with zero acceleration means each comet coasts to a stall at `velocity / drag` and hangs there fading, so hard hits reach further and soft ones die near the bottom. The chain runs backwards up the detector: the envelope drives `M#.smoothing`, so immediately after a hit the band is smoothed heavily and the detector goes briefly deaf, then sharpens again as the tail decays. That is a gate's hold time, and it stops a snare inside the kick's decay from launching a second comet on top of the first. Ember run for the comets, cobalt for the bed -- the one cold thing on the strip is the thing they travel over. Plays on Left, Right only

features.key: Looks | Mirror Brush Port of `mirror_brush`: a brush that paints while the room is loud, and whatever it painted scrolls outward from the centre, mirrored. The previous port was one line under a mirror on a triangle LFO, which is a shape bouncing rather than a trail being laid down. A TRAIL IS PARTICLES WITH A RATE, not a spawner with a trigger. `particles.rate` is a continuous stream in shapes per second, carried across frames so it means the same at # FPS as at #, and the audio band drives it -- so loud paints densely, quiet paints nothing, and the brush going down and up is the band crossing its squelch. That is what makes `threshold` a real knob here: it IS the squelch. `mirror` maps a screen position to `|pos - centre| * #`, so the emitter works in a half-strip where source # is the middle and source # is both ends. Every distance doubles with it: the animation's `min_speed` of #.# strip/s is #.# in this space, and the knob's ends are its declared #.#-# doubled. The animation's own comment says it folds with `abs(pos - #.#)`; this is that fold as a warp. `colors` cycling one entry per stroke becomes `colouring: random`, a draw held for the life of each particle. Consecutive strokes therefore differ, but not in the animation's fixed rotation. `react_speed` and `react_brightness` are toggles and do not port, for the reason `#-perlin-audio` gives -- both default false, so this takes the constant each selects and the reaction lands on density instead. `max_speed` is then the depth of a row that is not there. `bloom` is the animation's falloff either side of a painted SEGMENT and here it is a particle's whole half-extent, which is a different measurement of the same softness.

features.key: Looks | Ocean Swell Long swells rolling along the strip with a shorter chop riding on them and foam catching the light. Two `wave` emitters at different wavelengths travel in opposite directions, each scrolled by a translate on a full unipolar ramp so the scroll never has a seam; where they cross, the water heaves. The chop is a `ripple` warp on the long swell, its amount breathing on a slow sine. A perlin LFO drives the main scroll's rate, so sets of waves surge and ease rather than arriving like a conveyor, and a very slow sine stretches and compresses the wavelength itself. Foam is a fine, fast noise whose palette is black until its highest crests, where it turns near-white.

features.key: Looks | Echo Every kick throws a comet outward from the centre, and the room throws it back twice: once after Echo Gap, and again after twice that, each fainter and a shade further toward violet. The echoes are `delay` nodes. `M#` delays the kick's edge, and `M#` delays `M#`'s, so one Gap knob spaces both and the second echo always lands at twice the first. A delay keeps a queue, so a kick arriving while an echo is still on its way adds another rather than cancelling it. Each delay also CARRIES a value: `M#` reads the bass band on the frame the kick arrives and publishes that reading on the frame its echo leaves, and `M#` carries `M#`'s on again. That value sets the echo's launch speed, so a hard kick's echoes fly as far as the kick did -- without the carry, an echo would launch at whatever the music happened to be doing a third of a second later. features.key: Looks | Echo Every kick throws a comet outward from the centre, and the room throws it back twice: once after Echo Gap, and again after twice that, each fainter and a shade further toward violet. The echoes are `delay` nodes. `M#` delays the kick's edge, and `M#` delays `M#`'s, so one Gap knob spaces both and the second echo always lands at twice the first. A delay keeps a queue, so a kick arriving while an echo is still on its way adds another rather than cancelling it. Each delay also CARRIES a value: `M#` reads the bass band on the frame the kick arrives and publishes that reading on the frame its echo leaves, and `M#` carries `M#`'s on again. That value sets the echo's launch speed, so a hard kick's echoes fly as far as the kick did -- without the carry, an echo would launch at whatever the music happened to be doing a third of a second later.

Each band is its own layer cut to its stretch of the strip by a soft `window` gate, so the bands blend where they meet -- the sea into wet sand, the sand into a glowing horizon. A sine of about # minutes sinks it towards the sand and dims it, and the same sine walks the sky's `indexBias` so the clouds turn crimson as it sets and amber again as it rises. A second perlin wanders that bias on its own, so no two dusks match. Tide moves the whole shoreline -- sea edge, foam and sand -- up or down the strip. features.key: Looks | Black Hole Two bodies drift toward each other on opposed LFOs and detonate when they touch. What makes it possible is that the separation is read off the SHAPES -- `math abs_diff` on `L#.emitter.centre` and `L#.emitter.centre` -- rather than off the oscillators driving them. So the glow answers to where the bodies actually are, and it keeps answering if you grab the drift macro and move them by hand, which a patch built on the LFO outputs could not do. M# is the contact: `lt` against the merge distance, latching with hysteresis so a graze fires once rather than stuttering, and firing an EDGE so it can kick the particles directly without a threshold node in between. M# adds the two centres and the row halves it, so the burst happens at the midpoint and travels with it.
